  • Purpose: To provide guidelines instruction for management of situation wherein there is a shortage of bed in the hospital.
  • Scope: Hospital Wide
  • Responsibility: Administrator and Emergency Medical Officer
  • Policy:
  • Patients are admitted to the hospital through the emergency department and also the outpatient department.
  • All patients reaching the emergency department are provided with first aid and all available life saving measures.
  • Patients are then transferred to the respective in patient departments (wards) after being seen and advised by the consultant.
  • Patients seen in outpatient departments by the consultant are advised admission based on the clinical conditions.
  • All the admissions during 8.00 am to 7.00 pm are routed through admission counter located at the main entrance of the hospital.
  • All admissions after 7.00 pm are routed through the emergency department.
  • In case of non-availability of beds inside the inpatient care wards, patients are placed in the emergency ward till the beds are available as per the entitlement.
  • In case of non-availability of beds inside the semiprivate/private patients are placed in the general wards till the beds are available as per the entitlement.
  • Once any bed becomes vacant in the entitled category, patients are shifted to their entitled class, after filling up the transfer form through admission desk.
  • In case of absolute non-availability of beds, the hospital will take the initiative to transfer the patients to the nearest hospital or medical college by ambulance accompanied by a nurse or a doctor depending on the need.
  • Beds are categorized into general wards (male and female), semiprivate wards and private wards.
